standard_prerequisites.name: Permanence of separated and finite type morphisms under base change and composition
standard_prerequisites.reference: Morphisms, Stacks tags 01T4 and 01T3, and Schemes, Stacks tag 01KU, invoked at proof lines 96-103
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives separatedness and finite typeness of the structure morphism of the product directly from the corresponding properties of X and Y.

core_obligations: Show that X x_{Spec(k)} Y -> Spec(k) is of finite type and separated, as the composite of the base change X x_k Y -> Y of X -> Spec(k) with the separated finite type morphism Y -> Spec(k) (proof lines 96-103).

Reduce integrality of the product to the affine case: pick finite affine open coverings X = union U_i and Y = union V_j and conclude from the integrality of every U_i x_k V_j that the product is reduced and irreducible, hence integral (proof lines 104-113).

Prove the algebraic statement that A ⊗_k B is a domain whenever A and B are finitely generated k-algebras that are domains: assume a product of two nonzero tensors is zero, normalise the coefficients so that b_1, ..., b_n and d_1, ..., d_m are k-linearly independent and a_1, c_1 are nonzero, choose by the Nullstellensatz a maximal ideal m ⊂ A with m in the nonempty open D(a_1c_1) and A/m = k, and obtain the contradiction by reducing the relation modulo m (proof lines 115-140).
proof_roadmap: Separatedness and finite type: X x_k Y -> Y is a base change of the finite type morphism X -> Spec(k), and Y -> Spec(k) is separated and of finite type, so the composite X x_k Y -> Y -> Spec(k) has both properties (proof lines 96-103).

Affine reduction: choose finite affine open coverings X = union_{i} U_i and Y = union_{j} V_j; it is enough to make each U_i x_k V_j integral, because reducedness, irreducibility and integrality are checked on the members of an open covering (proof lines 104-113).

Algebraic core: for finitely generated k-algebras A, B that are domains, suppose (sum a_i ⊗ b_i)(sum c_j ⊗ d_j) = 0 with both factors nonzero in A ⊗_k B, and normalise so that b_1, ..., b_n and d_1, ..., d_m are k-linearly independent and a_1, c_1 are nonzero (proof lines 116-127).

Nullstellensatz step: since D(a_1c_1) is a nonempty open of Spec(A), the Nullstellensatz gives a maximal ideal m ⊂ A contained in D(a_1c_1) with A/m = k, so the relation may be evaluated at the residue classes a-bar_i, c-bar_j in k (proof lines 127-133).

Contradiction: the evaluated relation (sum a-bar_i b_i)(sum c-bar_j d_j) = 0 in B contradicts the k-linear independence of the b_i and the d_j together with B being a domain, completing the affine case and the lemma (proof lines 134-140).
difficulty_reason: The lemma claims that over an algebraically closed field the product of two varieties is again a variety, i.e. integral, separated and of finite type over k (statement lines 90-92). After the finite-affine-covering reduction the whole content sits in the affine statement that A ⊗_k B is a domain for finitely generated k-domains A and B: the proof assumes a zero product of two nonzero tensors, normalises the coefficients to k-linearly independent families b_i and d_j with a_1, c_1 nonzero, and then consumes algebraic closedness of k at exactly one point, namely the Hilbert Nullstellensatz applied to the nonempty open D(a_1c_1) to obtain a maximal ideal m with A/m = k (proof lines 118-131). Evaluating the tensor relation at m then contradicts k-linear independence and the fact that B is a domain (proof lines 132-140). The step is not formal: over a non-algebraically-closed field the corresponding maximal ideal need not have residue field k, and the statement really fails there, as the chapter's own example example-product-not-a-variety at lines 70-77 shows.

compared: public 576-589 (source stacks-project:varieties.tex, older snapshot): they count connected components under field extension, descent of ampleness, birational morphisms near normal points, completed local presentations, normalization under field extension, integral closures of ground fields, Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity, extension of line bundles, affineness or projectivity of curves and Euler characteristics; none of them states that the product of two varieties over an algebraically closed field is a variety.

public 197537 (arxiv, 'Semilattice sums of algebras and Maltsev products of varieties'): its 'products of varieties' are products in the universal-algebra sense of equational classes, not scheme-theoretic fibre products of varieties, so the phrase overlaps but the mathematical object does not.

No public item, retired claim or worklist row was found whose title or claim mentions the tensor product of two finitely generated domains over an algebraically closed field, which is the algebraic content of this lemma.
